lead: A coupling joins the ends of two shafts so that torque passes from one to the other, for example from a motor to a pump. A rigid coupling holds the shafts in exact line and is simple and strong, but it passes every misalignment into the bearings. A flexible coupling allows a small parallel, angular or axial error and softens shock. The design follows the torque through every part (shaft, key, hub, flange, bolts or pins) and checks each for shear, crushing or bearing pressure.
prereq: You need: the key checks in keys, keyways and splines.

sections.h3: Rigid couplings: sleeve, clamp and flange

items: Sleeve (muff) coupling: a cast-iron sleeve keyed over both shaft ends. Usual proportions: outer diameter D = 2d + 13 mm and length L = 3.5d. The sleeve is checked as a hollow shaft in torsion. It is cheap, but one shaft must be moved to remove it.
Clamp (split-muff) coupling: the sleeve is split along the axis and bolted round the shafts, so it can be fitted without moving them; friction and the key share the torque.

Flange coupling: a flange keyed on each shaft, the two flanges bolted face to face. The protected type has a rim that covers the bolt heads and nuts, so nothing projects to catch clothing. The marine type has the flanges forged on the shafts.

blocks.text: Usual proportions of a cast-iron protected flange coupling for shaft diameter d: hub diameter 2d, hub length 1.5d, bolt pitch circle diameter D<sub>1</sub> = 3d, flange outer diameter 4d, flange thickness t = 0.5d, protecting rim 0.25d. The torque path is shaft → key → hub → flange → bolts → second flange → key → second shaft, and each link has its own check:

items: Shaft: τ = 16T/(πd³). Hub as a hollow shaft: τ = 16T D/(π(D⁴ − d⁴)) with D = 2d.
Key: shear and crushing, as for any sunk key, over the hub length.
Flange shear at the hub: T = πD²tτ/2.
Bolts (fitted in reamed holes): force per bolt F = 2T/(nD<sub>1</sub>); shear τ = F/(πd<sub>b</sub>²/4); crushing σ<sub>c</sub> = F/(d<sub>b</sub> t).

blocks.text: Use the design torque T = K<sub>s</sub> × rated torque, with a service factor K<sub>s</sub> of about 1.25 to 1.5 for a smooth pump and 2 or more for a crusher.
Shafts never stay in perfect line: foundations settle and hot machines grow. Misalignment has three parts: parallel offset of the axes, angular misalignment and axial float.

items: Bushed-pin flexible coupling: a flange coupling whose bolts are replaced by pins carrying rubber bushes in one flange. The rubber deflects, so the coupling takes small parallel and angular errors and damps shock. The pin force is F = 2T/(nD1); the bush is sized for a bearing pressure of about 1 N/mm²: F = p Db lb; the pin is checked in shear and in bending, since F acts at the middle of the bush, away from the flange.
Oldham coupling: two slotted hubs and a centre disc with two tongues at 90°; it allows a parallel offset.

Universal (Hooke’s) joint: two yokes on a cross; it allows a large angle, but one joint gives an output speed that fluctuates twice per turn. Two joints with equal angles and the yokes in phase cancel the fluctuation, as on a truck propeller shaft.
Gear, grid, disc and jaw couplings are chosen from maker tables by torque, bore and speed.

blocks.text: A flexible coupling is not a cure for poor installation. Align the shafts first with a dial gauge or laser, allowing for the hot growth of the machine.

examples.question: Design a cast-iron protected flange coupling for a steel shaft transmitting 15 kW at 200 rpm. Allowable stresses: shaft, key and bolts 40 MPa in shear and 80 MPa in crushing; cast iron 15 MPa in shear. Use four bolts and the usual proportions.
steps: Proportions: hub diameter 100 mm, hub length 75 mm, D<sub>1</sub> = 150 mm, outer diameter 200 mm, flange t = 25 mm, rim 12.5 mm.

Key 14 × 9 for a 50 mm shaft, force F = 2T/d = 28 648 N. Over 75 mm: τ = 28 648/(14 × 75) = 27.3 MPa (safe), σ<sub>c</sub> = 28 648/(4.5 × 75) = 84.9 MPa, above 80 MPa. Make the hub and key 80 mm long: σ<sub>c</sub> = 79.6 MPa.
Flange shear at the hub: τ = 2T/(πD²t) = 2 × 716 200/(π × 100² × 25) = 1.82 MPa ≤ 15 MPa.
examples.answer: Shaft 50 mm; hub 100 mm × 80 mm; key 14 × 9 × 80 mm; four M10 fitted bolts on a 150 mm circle; flange 25 mm thick, outer diameter 200 mm, rim 12.5 mm.

examples.question: A bushed-pin coupling for a 30 kW, 720 rpm drive has six pins on a 160 mm pitch circle. Each pin is 14 mm in diameter and carries a rubber bush of 30 mm outer diameter; the pin load acts at the middle of the bush, 20 mm from the flange face. The bush pressure must not exceed 1 N/mm². Find the bush length and the stresses in the pin.
steps: Bush length: l<sub>b</sub> = F/(pD<sub>b</sub>) = 829/(1 × 30) = 27.6 mm; adopt 30 mm.
Combined: τ<sub>max</sub> = √((61.5/2)² + 5.4²) = 31.2 MPa, well within a steel pin’s limit.
examples.answer: Bush length 30 mm. The pin is stressed mainly in bending (61.5 MPa), not shear (5.4 MPa), which is why the bending check matters.

traps: Using the pitch circle diameter where the radius belongs: F = T/(nR) = 2T/(nD<sub>1</sub>). Mixing them halves or doubles the bolt force.
Checking the bolts in shear only. Flange crushing on the bolt, the hub and the flange shear at the hub are all part of the answer.
Checking a bushed pin in shear only. The force acts at the middle of the bush, so the pin also bends, and bending usually governs.
Forgetting the service factor, or using the rated torque for some checks and the design torque for others.
Saying a single universal joint gives a constant output speed. It needs a second joint at the same angle, in phase.

quiz.q: Name three rigid and three flexible couplings.
quiz.a: Rigid: sleeve (muff), clamp (split-muff), flange. Flexible: bushed-pin, Oldham, universal joint (also gear and jaw couplings).

quiz.q: Give the usual proportions of a muff coupling.
quiz.a: Sleeve outer diameter D = 2d + 13 mm and length L = 3.5d, where d is the shaft diameter.

quiz.q: Why is the flange coupling of a workshop line shaft usually the protected type?
quiz.a: The rim covers the bolt heads and nuts, so nothing projects from the spinning flange to catch clothing or a hand; it also guards against a loose bolt flying out.

quiz.q: A 15 kW, 960 rpm motor drives through a flange coupling with K<sub>s</sub> = 1.5 and four bolts on a 100 mm pitch circle. Find the design torque and the force on each bolt.
What misalignment does an Oldham coupling allow, and what does a universal joint allow?
quiz.a: Oldham: parallel offset between the axes. Universal joint: a large angle between the axes.

quiz.q: Six bushed pins on a 160 mm circle carry 829 N each. What torque does the coupling carry, and what bush length gives 1 N/mm² with a 30 mm bush?
A rigid coupling joins a motor to a pump, and the pump bearings fail every few months. Analyse and recommend.
quiz.a: A rigid coupling forces any offset or angle into the shafts, so the bearings carry a large extra radial load at every turn and their life falls. Check the alignment hot and cold with a dial gauge or laser, correct the soft foot, and fit a flexible (bushed-pin or disc) coupling rated for the remaining error.

beyond: Makers size couplings from tables of torque, bore, speed and service factor rather than by hand. Disc and diaphragm couplings with no lubrication drive turbines and compressors; torque-limiting and magnetic couplings protect machines from overload. Laser alignment systems now measure offset and angle in minutes. Search for "coupling service factor table" and "laser shaft alignment".

spec.aria: Section of a flange coupling joining two 50 millimetre shafts. Each shaft has a hub of 100 millimetres diameter and 80 millimetres length and a flange 25 millimetres thick and 200 millimetres across, with a protecting rim. Bolts cross both flanges at a 150 millimetre pitch circle. A box gives the bolt force 2387 newtons.
